notes:
Spectrum analyser front panel: the Spectrum device, the spectrum in the analyser overlay and the Visualizer's spectrum now read like a bench analyser: a 10 by 10 grid with the reference level on the top line, start and stop frequency, resolution, averaging and detector in the corners, the live trace in yellow and the max hold in cyan, marker 1 on the strongest peak and a second marker with the difference in frequency and level. Levels are now true dBFS (a sine reads its peak level).
Piano roll: with a scale chosen, the rows in the key are lighter and the others darker, every root row has a thin amber line, a note outside the key gets a dotted amber ring (and says so, for example "G♯4 outside A minor"), the chords under the clip (Am, F, C, G7 ...) are named in the ruler, and the keys are narrower with every note named beside them (root in amber, notes outside the key in grey).
Fixed: AudioLab no longer clicks around by itself when a MIDI port loops back (for example an IAC Driver port named "Ableton Push to Cubase"). A Push, Mackie, HUI, Launchpad or APC now only takes control after you tick Control surface for it in Controllers; AudioLab ignores its own messages coming back, stops a port that loops and tells you, and Controllers has a Stop all controllers switch. The update window keeps its buttons in view with long notes.
Fix clashes from the mixer: click a magenta clash cable and choose Duck (the quieter channel ducks under the louder one, only in that band, only while it plays) or Notch (a 2 dB cut there on its Pro EQ). The Ducker has a new button too: Only this band.
Loudness history: the loudness pop-up (click the LUFS box in the top bar) shows the last 30 seconds as a graph: the short-term loudness as a line that turns yellow above your target band and red more than 3 LU above it, the momentary loudness faint behind it, the integrated loudness dashed and the target band shaded green. The small graphs in the top bar and in the mixer's master box, and the Loudness and Meter devices, draw it the same way; the loudness range is marked as settling for its first 60 seconds.
Clashes in the mixer: turn on Clashes under the mixer's cables (or run "Show clashes between tracks in the mixer") and a magenta cable joins two channels that fight in the same frequency band where the playhead is, labelled with the band, thicker for a bigger clash. Click one for the numbers.
Level meters show peak and average in one bar: the bright part is the average level (RMS over 300 ms), the fainter part above it reaches the peak. The master strip in the mixer shows the RMS and the crest factor (how far the peaks stand above the average), and so do the tooltips of the channel peak read-outs and the transport's peak box. The mixer's meter view and the big meter in Settings now use the fader's scale.
Menus now fade in and out very briefly (90 ms in, 60 ms out) instead of popping. Nothing else changes yet: this is the groundwork for the new menus, dialogs, tooltips and notifications you picked. With reduced motion, Motion set to Signal only, or in Light mode they still appear at once.
Linked clips: make a linked copy of a clip (Alt+Shift-drag, or right-click › Duplicate as linked copy) and editing the notes or envelopes of one changes every copy. A small chain mark shows which clips are linked; Make unique breaks the link, Select linked copies finds them. Audio clips share their gain and warp. In the Fractals song the repeated Kick and Bass clips are already linked. Shift-drag still makes a plain copy.
Audio clips now show their sound in three colours: lows (kick, bass) in blue, mids (voices, most instruments) in amber and highs (hats, air) in white, so you can tell what is in a clip at a glance. The bands are worked out once per audio file in the background; the Live, FL, Cubase, Logic and Bitwig looks keep their usual waveform.
Launchpad and APC grids: a Novation Launchpad (Mini MK3, X, Pro MK3) or an Akai APC (APC40 MK2, APC mini, APC mini mk2) now lights up with your song's sections, 8 tracks across, and launches them from the pads and the buttons on the right, like the Push's Session mode. Launchpads also play notes in key (Keys or Note) and a 4x4 drum kit (Drums); APC faders move the track levels (they catch the level first, so nothing jumps), and the APC40's knobs, track buttons, transport and tempo knob work too.
Clips look quieter: no coloured title bar any more. Each clip has a thin line in its track colour along the top, its name on the clip in a lighter tone of that colour, and a darker body, so notes and waveforms stand out. Clicking and dragging work as before; the Live, FL, Cubase, Logic and Bitwig looks keep their title bars.
Settings search got smarter: it knows other words for things ("latency" finds Buffer size, "sound card" finds Output device), shows where each result lives (for example Sound › Audio › Audio driver), and also finds options that live outside Settings, like the metronome, Capture, Snap or the mixer's Compact channels. Choose one and "Show me" closes Settings and lights it up where it is.
Settings has new pages: 13 short pages in four groups (Program, Working, Sound, Project) built from cards, with a strip of live numbers at the top (engine rate, buffer, CPU, frame rate, glass level and output; click one to open its page). Nothing was lost: every option moved whole to its new page, keeps its value, and the old page names still find it in the search.
New look details: a drafting grid of hairlines in the arrangement and piano roll, units in amber next to every value, yellow for everything selected, and denser tracks. Two new settings under Density and motion (Settings, Layout): Density (Dense, Today, Roomy) and Motion (Ambient, Signal and transitions, Signal only).
MIDI controllers, step 7: mixing surfaces. A Mackie Control or HUI surface (Behringer X-Touch, Icon, Mackie and others in that mode) now runs AudioLab: motor faders on 8 tracks and the master, knobs on pan or on the selected device, Mute, Solo, Rec and Select, banks, transport and the jog wheel, with track names and the song position on its displays. If yours is not found by its name, set it under Works as on the Controllers page.
MIDI controllers, step 6: keyboards and pad controllers. Plug in an Akai MPK mini, Arturia MiniLab 3 or Novation Launchkey and its knobs move the device you have selected, its pads play the drum kit, nothing to set up. Any other controller: open Controllers, pick a template and press Set up by moving, then touch each knob, fader, pad and button in turn. Save a setup as your own template; Play, Stop and Record on most keyboards work too.
New: the frequency map (command list: Frequency map). One picture of the whole song: time across, pitch from 20 Hz to 20 kHz up, every spot in the colour of the track that is loudest there, with the sections on top. Point at a spot to read it, click to jump there and select that track, or show one track or group glowing over the rest. It measures in the background the first time and remembers it.
Behind the scenes for the frequency map: AudioLab can now measure every track beat by beat (how loud it is in each band from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, in the middle and at the sides, loudness, brightness and its strongest notes), quietly in the background and remembered between sessions. The map that shows it comes next.
MIDI controllers, step 5: Session mode on your Ableton Push 1. Press Session: the pads show 8 tracks across and the song's sections down, lit where a track plays something; the buttons on the right (and the pads) launch a section: from a stop it plays from there, while playing it jumps at the next bar (or at the end of the section, or at once: the Launch setting on the Controllers page; Shift+button: at once). Press the waiting section again to cancel; Note goes back.
Glass for the transport and the device panel: both now float a little in from the window edges with rounded corners, so you see the arrangement around them; the bottom-left corner is properly frosted again, and the transport gets the lens, with a little extra bend on its top and bottom edges.
